chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, among the most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah is the one to whom acts of kindness are made beloved, and to whom performing them is made beloved.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.أَحَبِّ عِبَادِ اللَّهِ: The most beloved of Allah's servants

ai.seo_question: Who are the most beloved servants to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the virtue of *al-ma'ruf* (kindness/goodness) is elevated beyond mere obligation to a beloved trait of the heart, indicating that divine love is attracted to those who naturally cherish and actively perform good deeds. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and the internalization of worship, where the act itself becomes a source of spiritual delight rather than just duty. The hadith underscores that true piety involves both an emotional affinity for goodness and its consistent practical application.
